summary: The contradiction argument is valid. Under I dominance the accepted defect bound yields the stated lower bound on the nonexceptional bad-edge mass S. If the affine rank of the positive bad-triangle midpoint set were at most two, applying the accepted support-free affine-slice bound to each reflected neighbor slice gives a uniform endpoint-degree bound, hence S <= 32G. The resulting constants force R+G >= 88Q/8499 > Q/100, contradicting the hard inequality. All uses of the predecessor facts, positivity, parity-class counting, degenerate ranks, and strict inequalities are consistent.
